question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

An excellent career _______ has now arisen with a leading recruitment agency.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. opportunity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Opportunity" means a favourable chance or occasion for doing something. The collocation "career opportunity" (a chance to advance in one's profession) fits perfectly with "has now arisen with a leading recruitment agency". (अवसर)

◦ Correct: An excellent career opportunity has now arisen with a leading recruitment agency.

• The verb "arise" naturally collocates with chance/opportunity/problem — "an opportunity has arisen".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "preferability" — the quality of being preferable; it is not used with "career" and does not fit "has arisen".

• Option 3 "division" — a separation into parts or a department; "career division" is meaningless here.

• Option 4 "severance" — the ending of a connection, especially of employment ("severance pay"); it conveys the opposite of a new opening.

NOTE

• Common collocations with "career": career opportunity, career prospects, career growth, career path, career break. Remember "opportunity of/for" a thing but "opportunity to do" something.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

The rodeo is (great way to unite soldier's skills and build) esprit de corps.
option_1: a great way to unite soldiers' skills and build
option_3: great way to unite soldier's skills and building
option_4: a great way to unite an soldier's skill and build
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. a great way to unite soldiers' skills and build.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Three corrections are needed in the bracketed part:

◦ The singular countable noun "way" needs the article "a" — "is a great way".

◦ Since more than one soldier is involved, the plural possessive "soldiers'" (apostrophe after the s) is required, not the singular "soldier's".

◦ The two verbs after "to" must be parallel — "to unite ... and build" (both bare infinitives).

◦ Correct: The rodeo is a great way to unite soldiers' skills and build esprit de corps.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "No substitution required" is wrong because the printed segment lacks the article "a".

• Option 3 keeps the missing article and breaks parallelism with "buildING".

• Option 4 uses the wrong article "an soldier's" (before a consonant sound) and the singular "skill".

NOTE

• "Esprit de corps" (a French phrase) means a feeling of pride, fellowship and loyalty shared by the members of a group. (सामूहिक एकता की भावना)

• Possessive rule: singular → soldier's; plural ending in -s → soldiers'; irregular plural → children's.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'

I ate a few brown rice this morning.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. I ate a few.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Rice" is an uncountable (mass) noun. Uncountable nouns take "a little", not "a few". "A few" is used only with plural countable nouns.

◦ Correct: I ate a little brown rice this morning.

• Hence the error lies in the segment "I ate a few".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "brown rice" is a correct noun phrase (adjective + noun).

• "this morning" is a correct adverbial of time used with the simple past "ate".

NOTE

• Quantifiers:

◦ Countable — a few, few, many, several, a number of (a few books).

◦ Uncountable — a little, little, much, a great deal of, an amount of (a little water, much rice).

• Common uncountable nouns in SSC exams: rice, water, information, furniture, luggage, advice, news, bread, money, work.

question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Explicit
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Specific.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Explicit" means stated clearly, exactly and in detail, leaving no room for doubt. Its closest synonym among the options is "specific" (precise, clearly defined). (स्पष्ट / सुनिश्चित)

◦ Example: The teacher gave explicit/specific instructions about the project.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Perfect" means faultless or complete — it does not carry the sense of "clearly stated".

• Option 3 "Nebulous" means vague, hazy and unclear — it is the antonym of explicit.

• Option 4 "Vogue" means the current fashion or trend — unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of explicit: specific, clear, precise, unambiguous, categorical, definite.

• Antonyms of explicit: implicit, vague, nebulous, ambiguous, obscure.

• Note the pair explicit (clearly stated) vs implicit (implied, not directly stated).

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

A house of shelter for a dog
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Kennel.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "kennel" is a small shelter or house built for a dog (also a place where dogs are bred or boarded). (कुत्ते का घर)

◦ Example: The puppy slept peacefully in its kennel.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Barns" — large farm buildings used for storing grain or housing cattle.

• Option 3 "Den" — the hidden home or lair of a wild animal such as a lion, bear or fox.

• Option 4 "Hangar" — a large shed in which aircraft are kept.

NOTE

• Homes of animals (a favourite SSC one-word-substitution topic): dog – kennel; horse – stable; cow – byre/shed; pig – sty; bee – hive/apiary; bird – nest/aviary; rabbit – burrow/hutch; lion – den; eagle – eyrie; sheep – pen/fold.

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

A pair of Eurasian jays ______ over the forest yesterday.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. flew.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The adverb "yesterday" fixes the action in the simple past tense, so the second form (V2) of the verb is needed. The past form of "fly" is "flew" (fly – flew – flown).

◦ Correct: A pair of Eurasian jays flew over the forest yesterday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "did flew" is wrong — after the auxiliary "did" the base form (V1) is used ("did fly"), never V2.

• Option 3 "fly" is the present form and clashes with "yesterday".

• Option 4 "flown" is the past participle (V3) and needs a helping verb such as has/have/had.

NOTE

• Simple past is used with definite past time markers: yesterday, last night, in 1999, two days ago, then.

• Verb forms: fly – flew – flown; grow – grew – grown; know – knew – known; throw – threw – thrown.

• "A pair of" takes a singular verb in the present ("a pair of shoes is"), but the past form "flew" is the same for singular and plural.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

The waiter giving the diners some complimentary mints.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. gave the diners.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence as printed has no finite (main) verb — "giving" is a present participle and cannot work as the predicate on its own. A finite verb in the simple past, "gave", is required.

◦ Correct: The waiter gave the diners some complimentary mints.

• "Give" here takes two objects: the indirect object "the diners" and the direct object "some complimentary mints".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "give the diner" — the singular "diner" does not agree with the plural sense, and the present "give" does not suit the narrative past.

• Option 2 "given the diners" — a past participle also needs an auxiliary (has/had given).

• Option 3 "No improvement" is wrong because the original sentence is incomplete.

NOTE

• Every clause must contain a finite verb. Participles (-ing / -ed forms) are non-finite and need a helping verb: "is giving", "has given", "was given".

• Verb forms: give – gave – given. "Complimentary" means given free of charge (मुफ़्त), not to be confused with "complementary" (completing something).

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

To have an itching palm
option_3: To have an urge to slap
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. To be greedy for money.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to have an itching palm" means to be greedy for money; to be eager to receive money or bribes. (धन का लालची होना)

◦ Example: Do not expect any favour from that clerk — he has an itching palm.

• The phrase comes from the old superstition that an itching palm foretells the coming of money; Shakespeare used it in Julius Caesar ("Let me tell you, Cassius, you yourself are much condemned to have an itching palm").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 3 are literal or invented meanings and do not correspond to any standard idiom.

NOTE

• Related money idioms: "to line one's pockets" (to make money dishonestly), "to grease someone's palm" (to bribe), "to be rolling in money" (to be very rich), "to make a fast buck" (to earn money quickly and easily).

question: Choose the sentence with no spelling error.
option_1: They completely rely on your accessory.
option_2: They completely rely on your acessory.
option_3: They completlly rely on your accessory.
option_4: They completely relie on your accessory.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. They completely rely on your accessory.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• All three words are spelt correctly only in Option 1:

◦ "completely" = COM + PLETE + LY (the silent "e" of "complete" is retained before "-ly").

◦ "rely" = to depend on (रेली — निर्भर होना).

◦ "accessory" = AC + CES + SO + RY (double "c" and double "s").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 misspells "accessory" as "acessory" (single c).

• Option 3 misspells "completely" as "completlly".

• Option 4 misspells "rely" as "relie".

NOTE

• "Accessory" means an additional item that goes with something (a bag, belt, etc.) or, in law, a person who helps a criminal.

• Spelling tip for "-ly": add "-ly" to the whole adjective — complete + ly = completely; sincere + ly = sincerely; careful + ly = carefully.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Now its referring to the same/ big lug who met his fate/ thanks to David's slingshot.
option_3: big lug who met his fate
option_4: Now its referring to the same
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Now its referring to the same.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The segment needs the contraction "it's" (= it is), not the possessive determiner "its". The sentence requires the present continuous "it is referring".

◦ Correct: Now it's (it is) referring to the same big lug who met his fate thanks to David's slingshot.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "big lug who met his fate" is grammatically fine — "lug" is informal for a clumsy, big fellow.

• "thanks to David's slingshot." is correct; "thanks to" means "because of".

• Hence "No error" cannot be chosen.

NOTE

• its = belonging to it (The dog wagged its tail).

• it's = it is / it has (It's raining. It's been a long day).

• Similar confusables: your/you're, their/they're/there, whose/who's.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Mr. Sharma opened the door of the stove to ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. peek.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Peek" (verb) means to look quickly or secretly, especially through a small opening. Opening the stove door "to peek" (to take a quick look inside) is the only meaningful completion. (झाँकना)

◦ Correct: Mr. Sharma opened the door of the stove to peek.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "pike" — a long-bodied freshwater fish, or an old weapon with a pointed head.

• Option 3 "piece" — a portion or part of something (a noun).

• Option 4 "peak" — the pointed top of a mountain; the highest point.

NOTE

• Homophones to remember: peek (a quick look) – peak (summit) – pique (to annoy / a feeling of resentment).

• Related expressions: "take a peek", "peek out", "sneak peek" (an advance glimpse).

question:
Select the appropriate synonym for the underlined word.

My parents have been lying to me since I was a kid.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. misleading.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Here "lying" (from the verb "lie") means telling untruths / deliberately deceiving someone. Its closest synonym is "misleading" — giving someone a wrong idea or impression. (गुमराह करना / झूठ बोलना)

◦ Example: The advertisement was misleading — it lied about the product's benefits.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "framing" means falsely incriminating someone or shaping/enclosing something — not a synonym of lying.

• Option 2 "stopping" (halting) and Option 3 "crying" (weeping) are completely unrelated.

NOTE

• Note the two verbs "lie": lie – lied – lied (to tell an untruth) and lie – lay – lain (to recline). Also lay – laid – laid (to put something down).

• Synonyms of lying: deceiving, misleading, fibbing, being untruthful. Antonyms: being honest, being truthful, being candid.

question:
Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.

Subtracted
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Adjunct.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Subtracted" means taken away / deducted / removed from a whole. Its opposite sense is that of something added or joined on — which is exactly what "adjunct" conveys: a thing added to something else as a supplement. (घटाया गया का विलोम — जोड़ा गया / अनुपूरक)

◦ Example: The new wing is an adjunct to the main hospital building.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Separated" (set apart, detached) is close in sense to subtracted, not opposite.

• Option 2 "Recap" means to summarise or restate briefly — unrelated.

• Option 4 "Annihilatory" relates to complete destruction — again a "removing" idea, not an "adding" one.

NOTE

• Synonyms of subtract: deduct, take away, remove, withdraw. Antonyms: add, append, annex, adjoin, supplement.

• In grammar, an "adjunct" is an optional element of a sentence (usually an adverbial) that adds extra information.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

Helen Keller was borne on 27 June 1880 in Tuscumbia.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. was born on.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed expression for coming into the world is "was/were born" — spelt born, not "borne".

• With a complete date (27 June 1880) the preposition "on" is used.

◦ Correct: Helen Keller was born on 27 June 1880 in Tuscumbia.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "was birth on" — "birth" is a noun, not a past participle; it cannot follow "was".

• Option 3 "No improvement" is wrong because "borne" is the wrong spelling here.

• Option 4 "is borne in" — the present tense contradicts the year 1880, and "in" is wrong before a full date.

NOTE

• born = brought into life (He was born in Delhi). borne = carried/endured (She has borne the pain bravely; a water-borne disease).

• Prepositions of time: on + a date/day (on 27 June, on Monday); in + month/year/season (in June, in 1880); at + clock time (at 5 p.m.).

• Static GK: Helen Keller (1880–1968) was the deaf-blind American author and activist who wrote "The Story of My Life".

question: Choose the incorrectly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Obsreve.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Obsreve" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "observe", which means to watch carefully / to notice / to obey a rule or celebrate an occasion. (निरीक्षण करना / पालन करना)

◦ Spelling key: OB + SERVE (think of the word "serve" inside "observe").

◦ Example: Scientists observe the movement of the stars.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Club", "Bulb" and "Thunder" are all spelt correctly.

NOTE

• Word family: observe (verb), observation (noun — the act of watching), observant (adjective — quick to notice), observatory (a building for observing stars), observance (following a custom or law).

question:
Select the appropriate antonym for the underlined word.

We should have warned you that they were coming.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. imperiled.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• To "warn" someone is to tell them about a possible danger in advance so that they can avoid it — i.e., to protect them from harm.

• The opposite action is to "imperil" someone — to put them in danger or at risk. (चेतावनी देना का विलोम — संकट में डालना)

◦ Example: Reckless driving imperils the lives of pedestrians.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "waked" (woke up) is unrelated to the idea of danger.

• Option 3 "predicted" (foretold) is close in sense to warning about something ahead, so it is not an antonym.

• Option 4 "prepared" (made ready) supports, rather than opposes, the idea of warning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of warn: caution, alert, forewarn, admonish, apprise.

• Antonyms of warn: imperil, endanger, jeopardise, expose to risk.

• Related words: peril (danger), perilous (dangerous), imperil (to endanger).

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Despite of technological innovations and powerful analytical tools, nothing is happening.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Despite of technological innovations.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Despite" is itself a preposition and is never followed by "of". The correct forms are "despite + noun" or "in spite of + noun".

◦ Correct: Despite technological innovations and powerful analytical tools, nothing is happening.

◦ Also correct: In spite of technological innovations ... , nothing is happening.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "and powerful analytical tools," correctly continues the noun phrase begun by "technological innovations".

• "nothing is happening." is correct — "nothing" is a singular indefinite pronoun and takes the singular verb "is".

• Hence "No error" cannot be chosen.

NOTE

• Frequently tested redundancy errors in SSC: despite ~~of~~, discuss ~~about~~, order ~~for~~, request ~~for~~ (as a verb), reach ~~at~~, comprise ~~of~~, return ~~back~~, repeat ~~again~~, cousin ~~brother~~.

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

We are getting support from a ______ number of textile traders.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. large.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank sits between the article "a" and the noun "number", so an adjective in the positive degree is needed. "A large number of" is a fixed quantifier phrase used with plural countable nouns.

◦ Correct: We are getting support from a large number of textile traders.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "larging" is not an English word.

• Option 2 "largest" is a superlative and would demand "the" ("the largest number"), not "a".

• Option 3 "largely" is an adverb (meaning mostly) and cannot modify the noun "number".

NOTE

• "A large number of + plural noun + plural verb" (A large number of traders are supporting us).

• "The number of + plural noun + singular verb" (The number of traders is increasing).

• Degrees: large – larger (than) – the largest.

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

That can be seen through
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Transparent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Transparent" describes a material that can be seen through — one that allows light to pass so that objects behind it are clearly visible (e.g. clear glass, water). (पारदर्शी)

◦ Example: The office follows a transparent recruitment process. (figurative — open and clear)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "Opaque" means that cannot be seen through at all — the exact opposite.

• Option 1 "Defatigable" relates to being capable of being tired out — unrelated.

• Option 4 "Reverent" means showing deep respect — unrelated.

NOTE

• Optical trio: transparent (fully see-through — glass), translucent (lets light through but not a clear image — frosted glass, butter paper), opaque (no light passes — wood, metal).

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

To get on one's nerves
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. To irritate or provoke one.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to get on one's nerves" means to irritate, annoy or exasperate someone, especially by doing something repeatedly. (चिढ़ाना / परेशान करना)

◦ Example: His constant humming really gets on my nerves.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 3 are distractors with no idiomatic basis; none of them expresses annoyance.

NOTE

• Related "nerve" expressions: "to lose one's nerve" (to lose courage), "to have the nerve to" (to have the audacity), "a bundle of nerves" (a very anxious person), "nerves of steel" (great courage).

• Other idioms of annoyance: "to rub someone the wrong way", "to drive someone up the wall", "to ruffle someone's feathers".

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

The thought here is that because saliva is (1) ______ alkaline, stimulating it by chewing gum after eating (2) ______ help neutralize the acidity in your mouth and throat. (3) ______ a very small study from 2005 did (4) ______ some merit to this approach, the size of the study makes it difficult to (5) _____ any real conclusions.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. slightly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank comes before the adjective "alkaline", and only an adverb can modify an adjective. The adverb form is "slightly" (= to a small degree). (थोड़ा-सा)

◦ Correct: ... because saliva is slightly alkaline ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "slight" is an adjective; two adjectives cannot stack as "slight alkaline".

• Option 3 "slightest" is a superlative adjective and would need "the".

• Option 4 "slighter" is a comparative adjective and would need "than".

NOTE

• Adverb + adjective is a very common pattern: slightly acidic, highly effective, completely wrong, extremely cold.

• Science link: saliva has a pH of about 6.2–7.6, i.e., near neutral to slightly alkaline, which helps it buffer mouth acids.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

The thought here is that because saliva is (1) ______ alkaline, stimulating it by chewing gum after eating (2) ______ help neutralize the acidity in your mouth and throat. (3) ______ a very small study from 2005 did (4) ______ some merit to this approach, the size of the study makes it difficult to (5) _____ any real conclusions.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. may.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage is stating a possibility/hypothesis ("The thought here is that ..."), so the modal of possibility "may" is the best fit: chewing gum may help neutralize the acidity. (हो सकता है)

◦ Correct: ... stimulating it by chewing gum after eating may help neutralize the acidity ...

• After a modal, the bare infinitive "help" is used — which all four options would allow, so the choice rests on meaning.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "shall" expresses future intention/obligation, which is too definite for a tentative theory.

• Option 2 "need to" expresses necessity, changing the meaning entirely.

• Option 3 "could" also shows possibility but is weaker/more hypothetical; "may" is the standard choice for a present, real possibility in scientific writing.

NOTE

• Modals of possibility: may (a real possibility), might (a slighter possibility), could (theoretical possibility), must (near certainty).

• The subject here is the gerund phrase "stimulating it by chewing gum", which is singular.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

The thought here is that because saliva is (1) ______ alkaline, stimulating it by chewing gum after eating (2) ______ help neutralize the acidity in your mouth and throat. (3) ______ a very small study from 2005 did (4) ______ some merit to this approach, the size of the study makes it difficult to (5) _____ any real conclusions.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. While.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The two halves of the sentence are in contrast: the study did find some merit, but its small size prevents firm conclusions. The subordinating conjunction "While" (here meaning "although") introduces exactly this concession.

◦ Correct: While a very small study from 2005 did find some merit to this approach, the size of the study makes it difficult to draw any real conclusions.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "As" would mean "because", giving a cause–effect link that contradicts the sense.

• Option 3 "So" shows result, not contrast, and cannot open this dependent clause.

• Option 4 "Yet" is a coordinating/contrast word that joins two main clauses ("..., yet ...") and cannot begin the sentence in this structure.

NOTE

• Contrast connectors: while, although, though, even though, whereas, despite, in spite of, however, nevertheless.

• When a subordinate clause comes first, it is followed by a comma: "While X, Y.".

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

The thought here is that because saliva is (1) ______ alkaline, stimulating it by chewing gum after eating (2) ______ help neutralize the acidity in your mouth and throat. (3) ______ a very small study from 2005 did (4) ______ some merit to this approach, the size of the study makes it difficult to (5) _____ any real conclusions.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. find.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank follows the emphatic auxiliary "did". After do/does/did, the verb must always be in its base form (V1) — hence "did find".

◦ Correct: ... a very small study from 2005 did find some merit to this approach ...

• "did find" is the emphatic past, used here to concede that the study genuinely did show something.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "found" is V2 and cannot follow "did".

• Option 4 "finds" is the present third-person singular form — again impossible after "did".

• Option 1 "founded" is the past of "found" meaning to establish (as in "founded a company") — a different verb altogether.

NOTE

• find – found – found (to discover) vs found – founded – founded (to establish).

• After do/does/did/don't/doesn't/didn't, always use V1: "He didn't go", "She does like it", "They did come".

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

The thought here is that because saliva is (1) ______ alkaline, stimulating it by chewing gum after eating (2) ______ help neutralize the acidity in your mouth and throat. (3) ______ a very small study from 2005 did (4) ______ some merit to this approach, the size of the study makes it difficult to (5) _____ any real conclusions.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. draw.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The standard collocation is "to draw conclusions", meaning to arrive at / reach a judgement on the basis of evidence. (निष्कर्ष निकालना)

◦ Correct: ... the size of the study makes it difficult to draw any real conclusions.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "expel" means to force out or dismiss (from school, a country).

• Option 3 "sell" means to exchange for money — meaningless with "conclusions".

• Option 4 "repel" means to drive back or cause distaste.

NOTE

• Useful collocations with "draw": draw a conclusion, draw an inference, draw a comparison, draw attention, draw a line, draw the curtains.

• Synonymous expressions: "reach a conclusion", "arrive at a conclusion", "come to a conclusion".

question: Who ascended the throne after the death of Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mohammad bin Tughlaq.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq (Ghazi Malik), the founder of the Tughlaq dynasty (1320), died in 1325 when a wooden pavilion at Afghanpur collapsed on him. He was succeeded by his son Juna Khan, who took the title Muhammad bin Tughlaq. (मुहम्मद बिन तुगलक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Muhammad bin Tughlaq (1325–1351) is famous for his ambitious but failed experiments — the transfer of the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad (Devagiri) and the introduction of token currency of bronze/copper.

• The traveller Ibn Battuta visited India during his reign and was appointed Qazi of Delhi.

• Firoz Shah Tughlaq succeeded him in 1351; Mahmud Tughlaq was the last Tughlaq ruler, during whose reign Timur invaded India (1398).

NOTE

• Delhi Sultanate dynasties in order: Slave/Mamluk (1206–1290) → Khalji (1290–1320) → Tughlaq (1320–1414) → Sayyid (1414–1451) → Lodi (1451–1526).

• Khusrau Khan and Mubarak Khan (Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah) belonged to the preceding Khalji period.

question: The Pudhumai Penn scheme is launched by which state government?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Pudhumai Penn" (meaning "Modern Girl") scheme was launched by the Government of Tamil Nadu in September 2022. Under it, girl students who have studied from Class 6 to Class 12 in government schools receive ₹1,000 per month until they complete their higher education (degree/diploma/ITI). (पुधुमई पेन योजना — तमिलनाडु)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The scheme's official name is the "Moovalur Ramamirtham Ammaiyar Higher Education Assurance Scheme", named after the social reformer who campaigned against the devadasi system and child marriage.

• Its aim is to raise the gross enrolment ratio of girls in higher education and to check school dropouts among girls.

• A parallel scheme for boys from government schools, "Tamil Pudhalvan", was launched in 2023.

NOTE

• Tamil Nadu's capital is Chennai; its major welfare schemes include Amma Canteen, Pudhumai Penn and free bus travel for women.

question: The National Rural Employment Programme was merged with ______ in 1989.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jawahar Rozgar Yojana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In April 1989, the National Rural Employment Programme (NREP, 1980) and the Rural Landless Employment Guarantee Programme (RLEGP, 1983) were merged into the Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (JRY) — a single wage-employment programme for the rural poor. (जवाहर रोज़गार योजना — 1989)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Under JRY, the cost was shared 80:20 between the Centre and the States, and implementation was routed through the village panchayats, making it the first major programme handed to Panchayati Raj institutions.

• JRY was later restructured as the Jawahar Gram Samridhi Yojana (1999), which in 2001 merged with the Employment Assurance Scheme (1993) to form the Sampoorna Grameen Rozgar Yojana (SGRY).

• SGRY was finally subsumed under NREGA/MGNREGA (2005–06), which guarantees 100 days of wage employment per rural household per year.

NOTE

• Indira Awas Yojana (1985) was a rural housing scheme, now restructured as Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana – Gramin (2016).

question: Rukmini Devi was featured in India Today's list of '100 People Who Shaped India'. She was awarded with 'Padma Bhushan' in the year 1956 and the 'Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship' in 1967. She was associated with which of the following dance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatnatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rukmini Devi Arundale (1904–1986) was the legendary exponent and reviver of Bharatanatyam. She was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 1956 and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship in 1967. (भरतनाट्यम — रुक्मिणी देवी अरुंडेल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• She founded "Kalakshetra" at Adyar, Chennai, in 1936, an institution dedicated to the preservation of classical Indian dance and music; it is now a Institution of National Importance.

• She played a decisive role in bringing Bharatanatyam (then called sadir) out of the temples on to the public stage and in giving it social respectability.

• She was also a nominated member of the Rajya Sabha and a noted animal-welfare activist; she declined an offer to be nominated President of India in 1977.

NOTE

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu, based on the Natya Shastra of Bharata Muni.

• Eight classical dance forms: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

question: Suggi is a famous folk dance form of ______ state of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Suggi" (also called Suggi Kunitha) is a popular harvest folk dance of Karnataka, performed chiefly by the farming communities of the coastal and Malnad regions during the harvest season. ("सुग्गी" — कर्नाटक का लोक नृत्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other folk dances of Karnataka: Yakshagana, Dollu Kunitha, Veeragase, Kamsale, Huttari, Bhootha Aradhane.

• Folk dances of the other options: Chhattisgarh — Panthi, Raut Nacha, Karma, Saila; Punjab — Bhangra, Giddha, Jhumar, Malwai Giddha; Sikkim — Singhi Chham, Maruni, Chutkey, Yak Chham.

NOTE

• Karnataka's capital is Bengaluru; its classical dance/theatre form Yakshagana combines dance, music, dialogue and elaborate costume.

question: In India, a microfinance loan is defined as a collateral-free loan given to a household having an annual income of up to Rs ______ as of October 2022.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rs 3 lakhs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the RBI's Master Direction on Regulation of Microfinance Loans (2022), a "microfinance loan" is defined as a collateral-free loan given to a household having an annual household income of up to ₹3,00,000 (₹3 lakh). (माइक्रोफाइनेंस ऋण — वार्षिक घरेलू आय ₹3 लाख तक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The RBI harmonised the microfinance framework across all regulated entities — banks, Small Finance Banks, NBFC-MFIs and NBFCs — with effect from 1 April 2022, removing the earlier separate rural (₹1.25 lakh) and urban (₹2 lakh) income caps.

• The rules also cap the monthly loan repayment obligation of a household at 50% of its monthly income and prohibit any prepayment penalty or collateral.

• "Household" means husband, wife and their unmarried children.

NOTE

• Microfinance in India is dominated by the Self Help Group (SHG)–Bank Linkage Programme launched by NABARD in 1992, the largest microfinance programme in the world.

question: Which of the following is the richest source of vitamin C?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lemon.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Among the given options, "lemon" — a citrus fruit — is by far the richest source of Vitamin C (ascorbic acid). Citrus fruits such as lemon, orange, sweet lime and grapefruit are the classic dietary sources of this vitamin. (नींबू — विटामिन C)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is a water-soluble vitamin. Its deficiency causes scurvy (bleeding and spongy gums, delayed wound healing).

• It acts as an antioxidant, helps in the formation of collagen and greatly improves the absorption of iron from food.

• The richest natural source in India is Amla (Indian gooseberry); other good sources are guava, orange, tomato, capsicum and green chilli.

• Cow milk, potato and cucumber contain only very small quantities of Vitamin C.

NOTE

• Vitamins and deficiency diseases: A – night blindness; B1 – beriberi; B3 – pellagra; B12 – anaemia; C – scurvy; D – rickets/osteomalacia; K – delayed blood clotting.

• Water-soluble vitamins: B-complex and C; fat-soluble: A, D, E, K.

question: What type of energy conversion takes place in a battery?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chemical energy into electrical energy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A battery (electrochemical cell) works on redox (oxidation–reduction) reactions: the chemicals inside react and release electrons, so the stored chemical energy is converted into electrical energy. (रासायनिक ऊर्जा → विद्युत ऊर्जा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Common energy conversions asked in exams:

◦ Electric bulb — electrical → light (and heat).

◦ Electric motor — electrical → mechanical.

◦ Generator/dynamo — mechanical → electrical.

◦ Microphone — sound → electrical; loudspeaker — electrical → sound.

◦ Solar cell — light (solar) → electrical.

◦ Electrolysis — electrical → chemical (the reverse of a battery).

• While charging a rechargeable battery, the conversion is electrical → chemical.

NOTE

• The law of conservation of energy states that energy can neither be created nor destroyed; it can only be transformed from one form to another.

• The first electric battery, the voltaic pile, was made by Alessandro Volta (1800).

question: According to 2011 Census, which among the following union territories has the lowest sex ratio?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Daman and Diu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census of India 2011, Daman and Diu recorded the lowest sex ratio — 618 females per 1,000 males — the lowest of any State or Union Territory in India. (दमन और दीव — 618)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Sex ratios of the other UTs in 2011: Dadra & Nagar Haveli – 774; Chandigarh – 818; Andaman & Nicobar Islands – 876; Lakshadweep – 946; NCT of Delhi – 868; Puducherry – 1037.

• The very low ratio in Daman & Diu and Dadra & Nagar Haveli is largely due to the large male migrant industrial workforce.

• India's overall sex ratio in 2011 was 943; Kerala had the highest (1084) and Haryana the lowest among states (879).

NOTE

• Sex ratio = number of females per 1,000 males.

• The 2011 Census was the 15th national census and the 7th after Independence; its theme was "Our Census, Our Future". Census Commissioner: C. Chandramouli.

• Daman & Diu and Dadra & Nagar Haveli were merged into a single UT on 26 January 2020.

question: "Dreams From My Father" is an autobiography of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Barack Obama.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Dreams from My Father: A Story of Race and Inheritance" (published 1995) is the memoir/autobiography of Barack Obama, the 44th President of the United States and the first African-American to hold that office. (बराक ओबामा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Obama's other books: "The Audacity of Hope" (2006) and "A Promised Land" (2020).

• He served as US President from 2009 to 2017 and was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2009.

• He was the Chief Guest at India's Republic Day parade in 2015 — the first US President to be so honoured.

NOTE

• Famous autobiographies/diaries: "The Diary of a Young Girl" – Anne Frank; "The Autobiography of Benjamin Franklin" – Benjamin Franklin; "My Autobiography" – Benito Mussolini; "The Story of My Experiments with Truth" – Mahatma Gandhi; "Wings of Fire" – A. P. J. Abdul Kalam.

question: Which among the following songs was composed by famous Indian musician Rahul Dev Burman?
option_3: Kisi Ki Muskurahaton Pe Ho Nisar
solution_text:
The correct answer is Yeh Dosti Hum Nahi Todenge.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Yeh Dosti Hum Nahi Todenge", the celebrated friendship song from the film Sholay (1975), was composed by Rahul Dev Burman (R. D. Burman), with lyrics by Anand Bakshi and vocals by Kishore Kumar and Manna Dey. (आर. डी. बर्मन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• R. D. Burman (1939–1994), affectionately called "Pancham da", was the son of the composer S. D. Burman. He revolutionised Hindi film music with Western rhythms and innovative sounds in films such as Teesri Manzil, Amar Prem, Hare Rama Hare Krishna, Sholay, Masoom and 1942: A Love Story.

• The other songs: "Kesariya" — composed by Pritam (Brahmastra, 2022); "Kisi Ki Muskurahaton Pe Ho Nisar" — composed by Shankar–Jaikishan (Anari, 1959); "Ae Dil Hai Mushkil" — composed by Pritam (2016).

NOTE

• R. D. Burman won the Filmfare Award for Best Music Director for Sanam Teri Kasam, Masoom and (posthumously) 1942: A Love Story.

question:
The President of India shall be elected by the members of an electoral college consisting of:

I. The elected members of both Houses of Parliament

II. The elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neither I nor II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per Article 54 of the Constitution, the President is elected by an electoral college consisting of:

◦ the elected members of both Houses of Parliament, and

◦ the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States, and

◦ the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the Union Territories of Delhi and Puducherry (added by the 70th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992).

• Neither statement I alone nor statement II alone describes this electoral college, since the college is complete only when all three components are taken together — including the Delhi and Puducherry Assemblies, which both statements omit. Hence the official answer is "Neither I nor II".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Nominated members of Parliament and of the State Legislative Assemblies, and all members of the Legislative Councils (Vidhan Parishads), do not take part in the presidential election.

• The election is held by the system of proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote, and the voting is by secret ballot (Article 55).

• Disputes relating to the President's election are decided by the Supreme Court (Article 71).

NOTE

• Presidential provisions: Art. 52 (office of President), Art. 53 (executive power), Art. 54 (election), Art. 55 (manner of election), Art. 56 (term — 5 years), Art. 58 (qualifications — citizen of India, 35 years of age, qualified for election to the Lok Sabha), Art. 61 (impeachment).

question: In January 2022, India signed a USD 374.96-million deal with the ______, its single biggest defence export order.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Philippines.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In January 2022, India signed a USD 374.96 million contract with the Philippines for the supply of the BrahMos shore-based anti-ship supersonic cruise missile system — India's single biggest defence export order at the time. (फिलीपींस — ब्रह्मोस मिसाइल सौदा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• BrahMos is a supersonic cruise missile developed jointly by India's DRDO and Russia's NPO Mashinostroyeniya; its name comes from the rivers Brahmaputra and Moskva.

• It flies at about Mach 2.8–3.0, can be launched from land, sea, air and submarine platforms, and follows a "fire and forget" principle.

• The first batch of BrahMos missiles was delivered to the Philippines in April 2024.

NOTE

• India's defence exports crossed ₹21,000 crore in 2023-24. Key export items include the Dornier aircraft, Akash missile system, radars, and BrahMos. The government's target is ₹50,000 crore of defence exports by 2028-29.

question: Which component of the cell contains the hereditary material of the cell, the DNA?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nucleus.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "nucleus" is the component of the cell that contains the hereditary material, DNA, organised into chromosomes. It directs all cellular activities and is therefore called the "control room" or "brain" of the cell. (केंद्रक — डीएनए)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The nucleus is bounded by a double-layered nuclear membrane with nuclear pores, and contains the nucleolus (which makes ribosomes) and chromatin.

• Cell wall — a rigid outer covering made of cellulose, present only in plant cells; gives shape and protection.

• Cell membrane (plasma membrane) — a selectively permeable covering that controls the entry and exit of substances.

• Cytoplasm — the jelly-like fluid holding the organelles; the site of many metabolic reactions.

NOTE

• DNA (Deoxyribonucleic acid) carries genetic instructions; a functional segment of DNA is a gene. Its double-helix structure was described by Watson and Crick (1953).

• Robert Brown discovered the nucleus (1831); Robert Hooke discovered the cell (1665).

question: Megasthenes was a Greek ambassador in the court of ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chandragupta Maurya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Megasthenes was the Greek ambassador sent by Seleucus Nicator to the court of Chandragupta Maurya (reign c. 322–298 BCE) at Pataliputra. He wrote the account "Indica", which describes Mauryan society, administration and the capital city. (मेगस्थनीज़ — चंद्रगुप्त मौर्य के दरबार में)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Chandragupta Maurya founded the Maurya Empire in 322 BCE with the help of his mentor Chanakya (Kautilya/Vishnugupta), author of the Arthashastra.

• He defeated Seleucus Nicator around 305 BCE; the peace treaty gave him territories west of the Indus, and Seleucus sent Megasthenes as envoy.

• In his last years he is said to have embraced Jainism under Bhadrabahu and to have died at Shravanabelagola (Karnataka) by sallekhana.

NOTE

• Other foreign envoys/travellers: Deimachus (to Bindusara), Dionysius (to Ashoka, sent by Ptolemy Philadelphus), Fa-Hien (Chandragupta II), Hiuen Tsang (Harshavardhana), Al-Biruni (with Mahmud of Ghazni).

question: The Deccan Plateau is a triangular landmass in India that lies to the south of the river ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Narmada.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Deccan Plateau is a large triangular landmass in peninsular India lying to the south of the river Narmada. Its apex points southwards, with the Satpura range forming its northern edge. (नर्मदा नदी के दक्षिण में दक्कन का पठार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Boundaries of the Deccan Plateau: Western Ghats (Sahyadri) in the west, Eastern Ghats in the east, Satpura–Vindhya ranges and the Narmada valley in the north.

• It slopes gently from west to east, which is why most peninsular rivers (Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri, Mahanadi) flow eastwards into the Bay of Bengal.

• The Narmada and Tapi are the two major peninsular rivers flowing westwards through rift valleys into the Arabian Sea.

• The plateau is largely made of basaltic lava (Deccan Traps) and has fertile black (regur) soil, ideal for cotton.

NOTE

• The Narmada rises from Amarkantak (Madhya Pradesh); the Tapi rises from Multai (Betul, MP). Both are separated from the Deccan Plateau proper by the Satpura range.

question: In which sport, Bajrang Punia won a gold medal at the Commonwealth Games 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Wrestling.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bajrang Punia won a gold medal in wrestling (men's freestyle 65 kg) at the Commonwealth Games 2022 held in Birmingham, England. (कुश्ती — बजरंग पूनिया)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• This was Bajrang's second consecutive CWG gold (he had also won gold at Gold Coast 2018 and silver at Glasgow 2014).

• He won a bronze medal at the Tokyo Olympics 2020 (held in 2021) and is a World Championship medallist.

• He has been honoured with the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award (2019), the Arjuna Award (2015) and the Padma Shri (2019).

• India finished 4th at CWG 2022 with 61 medals (22 gold, 16 silver, 23 bronze); India's wrestlers alone won 12 medals (6 gold).

NOTE

• Other Indian gold medallists in wrestling at CWG 2022: Vinesh Phogat, Sakshi Malik, Ravi Kumar Dahiya, Deepak Punia and Naveen.

question: The first High Court in India was established in ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1862.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first High Courts in India were established in 1862 at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras, under the Indian High Courts Act of 1861. The Calcutta High Court, set up on 1 July 1862, is the oldest High Court in India. (1862 — कलकत्ता उच्च न्यायालय)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Indian High Courts Act, 1861 abolished the Supreme Courts (at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras) and the Sadar Adalats in the Presidency towns and merged their jurisdiction into the new High Courts.

• The Allahabad High Court was the fourth, established in 1866.

• Under the Constitution, Articles 214–231 deal with the High Courts; Article 214 provides for a High Court for each State, and Article 231 allows a common High Court for two or more States/UTs.

• Judges of a High Court hold office until the age of 62 years.

NOTE

• The Supreme Court of India was inaugurated on 28 January 1950, replacing the Federal Court (1937) and the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council. Supreme Court judges retire at 65.

question: Which of the following Rebellion occurred between 1855-56?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Santhal rebellion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Santhal Rebellion (Santhal Hul)" took place in 1855–56 in the Rajmahal hills region of present-day Jharkhand (then Bengal Presidency). It was led by the brothers Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu (along with Chand and Bhairav) against zamindars, moneylenders (dikus) and British officials. (संथाल विद्रोह — 1855-56)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The rebellion's immediate causes were oppressive revenue collection, land alienation and debt bondage imposed on the Santhals.

• After its suppression, the British created the separate "Santhal Parganas" district (1856) with special protective laws for tribal land.

• Dates of the other risings: Kol Rebellion – 1831-32 (Chhotanagpur, led by Buddho Bhagat); Ramosi Rising – 1822-29 (Maharashtra, led by Chittur Singh and Umaji Naik); Paika Rebellion – 1817 (Odisha, led by Bakshi Jagabandhu).

NOTE

• Other major tribal revolts: Munda Ulgulan (1899-1900) led by Birsa Munda; Bhil revolt (1818-31); Khond uprising (1837-56); Rampa rebellion (1922-24) led by Alluri Sitarama Raju.

question: The ancient harvest festival of Baisakhi is celebrated in which month of the year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is April.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Baisakhi (Vaisakhi)" is celebrated in the month of April, usually on 13 or 14 April. It marks the harvesting of the rabi crop and the beginning of the Punjabi/Sikh new year. (बैसाखी — अप्रैल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• For Sikhs, Baisakhi commemorates the founding of the Khalsa Panth by Guru Gobind Singh in 1699 at Anandpur Sahib.

• The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place on Baisakhi day, 13 April 1919, at Amritsar.

• The same day is celebrated across India under different names: Bihu (Assam), Poila Boishakh (West Bengal), Puthandu (Tamil Nadu), Vishu (Kerala), Bohag Bihu (Assam), Maha Vishuva Sankranti/Pana Sankranti (Odisha).

NOTE

• Major harvest festivals: Pongal & Makar Sankranti (January), Baisakhi (April), Onam (Aug–Sept), Nuakhai (Aug–Sept), Wangala (November).

question: Lionel Messi is a famous player of ______ sport.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Football.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lionel Messi, from Argentina, is one of the greatest football players of all time. He captained Argentina to victory in the FIFA World Cup 2022 in Qatar and was awarded the Golden Ball of that tournament. (फुटबॉल — लियोनेल मेसी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Messi spent most of his club career with FC Barcelona (Spain), then played for Paris Saint-Germain (France) and now plays for Inter Miami (USA).

• He has won a record number of Ballon d'Or awards, along with the Copa América (2021, 2024) and an Olympic gold (Beijing 2008).

NOTE

• Football's world governing body is FIFA (founded 1904, headquarters in Zurich, Switzerland); the World Cup is held every four years.

• Football terms: goal, penalty, corner kick, offside, dribble, hat-trick, free kick. India's football governing body is the AIFF, and the national team's biggest tournament is the AFC Asian Cup.

question: Ramappa Temple is dedicated to which God?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Shiva.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Ramappa Temple, also known as the Rudreshwara Temple, is dedicated to Lord Shiva. It stands at Palampet in the Mulugu district of Telangana. (रामप्पा मंदिर — भगवान शिव)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• It was built in 1213 CE by Recharla Rudra, a general of the Kakatiya ruler Ganapati Deva.

• It is the only temple in India known by the name of its sculptor, Ramappa.

• It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in July 2021, becoming the 39th Indian site on the list.

• Its famous features are the floating bricks used in the shikhara (so light that they float on water), the sandbox foundation technique and the highly polished black basalt pillars and madanika figures.

NOTE

• Other Telangana heritage attractions: Charminar and Golconda Fort (Hyderabad), Thousand Pillar Temple (Warangal) and the Warangal Fort, also built by the Kakatiyas.

question: Mosses and lichens are found in which kind of forest?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tundra Forest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mosses and lichens are the characteristic vegetation of the tundra region. In the extremely cold, treeless polar and high-altitude areas, the ground remains frozen (permafrost), so only very hardy, low-growing plants such as mosses, lichens and sedges can survive. (टुंड्रा — काई और लाइकेन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The tundra lies mainly in the Arctic region — northern Canada, Alaska, Greenland, Siberia and northern Scandinavia; alpine tundra occurs on high mountains.

• Animals of the tundra: reindeer/caribou, arctic fox, polar bear, musk ox, seal, walrus, snowy owl; the human inhabitants include the Eskimos (Inuit), Lapps/Sami and Yakuts.

• Tropical rain forests (evergreen, e.g. Amazon) have dense multi-storeyed vegetation; coniferous (taiga) forests have pine, fir and spruce; temperate deciduous forests have oak, ash and beech.

NOTE

• Lichen is a symbiotic association of an alga and a fungus and is a well-known bio-indicator of air pollution — it cannot survive where SO₂ pollution is high.

question: In which of the following articles, "Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment" is mentioned?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 16.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 16 of the Constitution guarantees "Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment" — no citizen shall be discriminated against in respect of any employment or office under the State on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth or residence. (अनुच्छेद 16)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Article 16(4) permits the State to make provision for the reservation of appointments in favour of any backward class not adequately represented in the services.

• Article 16(4A) (77th Amendment, 1995) allows reservation in promotion for SCs/STs; Article 16(6) (103rd Amendment, 2019) provides up to 10% reservation for the Economically Weaker Sections (EWS).

• The other Articles: Article 14 — equality before law and equal protection of the laws; Article 15 — prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth; Article 17 — abolition of untouchability; Article 18 — abolition of titles.

NOTE

• Articles 14 to 18 together constitute the Right to Equality, part of the Fundamental Rights (Articles 12–35, Part III) of the Constitution.

question: The ______ was started by the Sikh reformers to purify their religious places by removing the evil social practices that had slowly crept into them.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Akali Movement.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Akali Movement" (also called the Gurdwara Reform Movement) was launched by Sikh reformers in the 1920s in Punjab to free the gurdwaras from the control of corrupt mahants (hereditary priests) and to remove the evil social practices that had crept into these places of worship. (अकाली आंदोलन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The movement was non-violent in character, and its volunteers were organised into jathas; major episodes include the Nankana Sahib tragedy (1921), the Keys Affair (1921) and the Guru ka Bagh morcha (1922).

• It led the British to enact the Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925, which transferred the management of gurdwaras to the elected Shiromani Gurdwara Prabandhak Committee (SGPC, formed 1920).

• The Akali Dal (1920) emerged as the political wing of this movement.

NOTE

• The other options: the Namdhari (Kuka) Movement was founded by Bhagat Jawahar Mal and led by Baba Ram Singh (1857 onwards) for religious and social reform; the Nirankari Movement was started by Baba Dayal Das against idol worship and ritualism; the Ghadar Movement (1913) was a revolutionary movement started by Indians in North America under Lala Har Dayal and Sohan Singh Bhakna.
